sources.cite: CompTIA SecurityX CAS-005 (V5) exam page: domains Governance, risk, and compliance 20%, Security architecture 27%, Security engineering 31%, Security operations 22%
sources.note: Relevant text: Security architecture covers network architecture ('segmentation, microsegmentation, VPN, always-on VPN, and API integration'), Zero Trust ('defining subject-object relationships'), security boundaries ('asset identification, management, attestation, data perimeters, and secure zones') and deperimeterization ('SASE, SD-WAN, and software-defined networking'); Security operations covers incident response including root cause analysis. The page has no objective text on federation by name. Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-11; the CAS-005 objectives PDF was not re-read here. The course's unit titles are the course's own wording. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's federation-token-forgery (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.
The organization, the systems and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the security architect at Brightline Medical, a fictional maker of connected infusion pumps. A firmware release is due; the pipeline has no security gates and devices accept any firmware image.
handover: CI builds and ships firmware; tests are functional only.
Device-to-cloud traffic uses RSA-2048 keys burned in at manufacture with no rotation path.
howItWorks: The console shows the alert queue, the event log and each asset's status.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Check-in 2: the release includes a library with a known remote-code flaw; a hospital's scanner finds it on the pumps.
Check-in 3: a contractor's leaked token exposes the repository and its signing key.
Check-in 4: a key-extraction flaw in the chip is published; the fleet's keys can't be rotated.

choices.label: Add SAST, dependency scanning and an SBOM to CI, require two-person review on the release branch, and block on criticals
choices.feedback: DevSecOps builds security checks into every build and protects the release branch.

choices.label: Run a manual review before each release
choices.feedback: Better than nothing, but late and inconsistent.

choices.label: Ship and add security next quarter
choices.feedback: A vulnerable library ships to devices in hospitals.

signPrompt.title: Devices accept any image
signPrompt.context: An attacker on the update channel could push firmware.

choices.label: Sign releases with a key held in an HSM and make devices verify the signature (secure boot) before installing
choices.feedback: Code signing with verification on the device prevents malicious updates.

choices.label: Rely on TLS for the update channel
choices.feedback: TLS protects transport, not a malicious image from a compromised server.

choices.label: Sign with a key stored in the CI repository
choices.feedback: Anyone with repo access can sign malicious firmware.

cryptoPrompt.title: Keys with no rotation path
cryptoPrompt.context: RSA-2048 keys are burned in; regulators expect post-quantum planning.

choices.label: Design key rotation over signed updates, an algorithm-agile protocol, and a migration plan to post-quantum algorithms

effects.log: A rotation and migration design is approved.

choices.feedback: Crypto agility lets algorithms and keys change without replacing devices.

choices.label: Move to RSA-4096 in the next hardware revision
choices.feedback: Still no rotation; still a hardware change.

choices.label: Leave keys as they are for the device's life
choices.feedback: A compromised key can never be replaced.

parts.label: Pipeline and firmware
parts.criteria: SAST, SCA, SBOM, protected review; HSM signing with on-device verification.
parts.modelAnswer: CI runs SAST, dependency scanning and an SBOM with two-person review; firmware is signed with an HSM key and verified on the pump.

parts.label: Crypto
parts.criteria: Rotation over signed updates and algorithm agility with a migration plan.
parts.modelAnswer: Keys rotate over signed updates and the protocol can change algorithms, with a post-quantum migration plan.
